'''Rembarrnga''' (Rembarunga) is an [[Australian Aboriginal language]]. It is one of the Northern [[Non-Pama–Nyungan languages]], spoken in the [[Roper River]] region of the [[Northern Territory]]. There are three dialects of Rembarrnga, namely Galduyh, Gikkik and Mappurn. It is a highly endangered language, with very few remaining fluent speakers. It is very likely that the language is no longer being learned by children. Instead, the children of Rembarrnga speakers are now learning neighbouring languages such as [[Australian Kriol language|Kriol]] in south central Arnhem Land, and [[Gunwinggu language|Kunwinjku]], a dialect of [[Bininj Kunwok]], in north central Arnhem Land.

Fluent speakers of Rembarrnga currently (2015) live in the remote towns of [[Maningrida, Northern Territory|Maningrida]] and [[Ramingining, Northern Territory|Ramingining]], and in nearby outstations such as Borlkdjam, Buluhkaduru and Malnyangarnak. Some other communities associated with Rembarrnga are Ankebarrbirri, Barunga, Beswick and Bulman. Neighbouring languages include Dalabon, Burarra, Ngalakan, Ngandi and the Bininj Kunwok dialects Kunwinjku and [[Kune dialect|Kune]].

Linguists who have worked with Rembarrnga speakers to produce language materials include Graham McKay, Carolyn Coleman and Adam Saulwick. Principal works on Rembarrnga include a grammar,<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title = Rembarnga : a language of central Arnhem Land|last = McKay|first = Graham|publisher = PhD Thesis, Australian National University|year = 1975|location = Canberra}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title = Aspects of the verb in Rembarrnga, a polysynthetic language of northern Australia: grammatical description, texts and dictionary|last = Saulwick|first = Adam|publisher = PhD Dissertation, University of Melbourne|year = 2003|location = Melbourne}}</ref> a dictionary<ref>{{Cite book|title = A first dictionary of Rembarrnga - compiled by Adam Saulwick; incorporating material recorded by Carolyn Coleman and Graham McKay|last = Saulwick|first = Adam|publisher = Maningrida Arts and Culture|year = 2003|location = Maningrida}}</ref> and a learner's guide.<ref>{{Cite book|title = A learner's guide to the Rembarrnga language|last = Saulwick|first = Adam|publisher = Maningrida Arts and Culture|year = 2003|location = Maningrida}}</ref>

* Stop sounds are voiced as [b, d, ɖ, ɟ, ɡ] when in word-initial position or following nasal sounds.
* A glottal stop [ʔ] is heard in syllable-final position when after vowels or sonorant sounds.
* /ɾ/ can also be heard as a trill [r] in intervocalic position.
